features.feature_value: Focused on whether language was useful/helpful and not mean-spirited.
features.evidence_span: focused on  the language used to determined if the posts were useful or helpful and not mean-spirited.
features.rationale: The reflection explicitly states a criterion centered on helpful/useful language versus mean-spiritedness.

features.feature_value: Tried to ignore political content and interpret content as venting vs argumentative.
features.evidence_span: I tried to ignore the political content. I looked for swearing and words that weren't about making an argument, but about venting anger.
features.rationale: The participant describes a specific approach to downweight politics and use intent/tone cues (venting anger).

features.feature_value: Attempted to stay bipartisan; rejected only outright attacks/degrading comments.
features.evidence_span: I tried to remain bipartisan when evaluating both views. I only rejected out right attacks or degrading comments made to the president or elected officials.
features.rationale: The reflection clearly identifies an evaluation stance (bipartisan) and a rejection threshold (attacks/degrading).

features.feature_value: Approved heated posts if respectful; removed posts with harmful language or unproductive conversation.
features.evidence_span: approving politically heated posts as long as they were remaining respectful... chose to remove posts that contained harmful language or just didn't promote productive conversation.
features.rationale: The participant provides explicit keep/remove rules based on respectfulness and whether language promotes productive dialogue.

features.feature_value: Removed vulgar posts and those based on conspiracy theories or unfounded self-serving opinions.
features.evidence_span: posts that were vulgar, based in conspiracy theories or in self-serving opinions not based in any facts got the boot.
features.rationale: The participant links removal to specific content types (vulgarity, conspiracy, lack of factual basis).

features.feature_value: Declined exceedingly combative/overly accusatory/low-quality posts; also felt annoyed reading conservative statements due to opposing their party.
features.evidence_span: It annoyed me to read the conservative statement, no matter what it was, because I am so opposed to their party.
features.rationale: The reflection explicitly includes an affective/attitudinal factor (annoyance tied to party opposition) alongside content quality cues.

features.feature_value: Objective moderation: removed insulting/demeaning posts; allowed constructive criticism.
features.evidence_span: I removed insulting and demeaning posts. I allowed constructive criticism posts.
features.rationale: The participant states a clear keep/remove distinction centered on whether posts are insulting vs constructive.

features.feature_value: Saw some as mere “Freedom of Speech,” while others as outright false misinformation.
features.evidence_span: Some of the statements were simply "Freedom of Speech" where others were outright false statements and mis-information.
features.rationale: The participant uses explicit content validity cues (false misinformation vs speech framing) to guide decisions.
